title: The agent offers the route instead of forcing a mask, and prompts an edit as verb plus target
description: Fabio, 2026-09-22, out of MPI-877 round 3. Round 3's two faults came back green - the edit landed as a history entry with latents drawing in the open workspace, and the prompt named nothing outside the mask - but the RESULT was still wrong, and the conversation that followed found three separate causes, none of them MPI-877's. (1) THE MASK IS FORCED. The Masking rule (`agentLoop.mjs:1162`) funnels every change confined to a region into a painted mask. Fabio: 'any edit can be just an edit. It doesn't need to be a localised edit ... The mask is more effective, but shouldn't always be forced on the user.' The test is whether the request names a PART of the picture: no part named ('make it night') runs whole-image with no question; a part named WITH preservation words ('without changing anything else', 'keep the size, only this area') goes straight to a mask, they already chose; a part named with no preservation words ('change the hair colour', 'change the pose') gets one line offering both, recommending the mask, and WAITS. Three bounds keep it from becoming a menu: at most three routes, one line each (op + model + why); only at a genuine fork; always recommend, never 'here are your options, which?'. (2) THE WORKED EXAMPLE IN THE SYSTEM PROMPT IS THE PROMPT THAT FAILED. `agentLoop.mjs:1162` teaches 'convert the boy into a demon: glowing red eyes, sharp horns, pale grey skin, a sinister grin' as the prompt the model 'needed'. It was never rendered before being written down. Fabio rendered it: the adjective list REPLACED the subject and lost the boy's likeness, while his own plain 'convert the boy into a demon version of himself' kept more of it. Swap the example for the one that worked, and state the shape: for the edit family the instruction is a VERB plus a TARGET, and adjectives are added only when the user named them. This is the highest-leverage line in the rule because the model copies it. (3) NO FALLBACK LADDER. Fabio found `inpaint` beat `kleinEdit` on this picture and a simpler prompt beat a longer one - 'different cases sometimes need different approaches'. Nothing in the rule says what to do when a masked result comes back wrong. It should: say which op and why before sending, and on a bad result reach for a DIFFERENT OP or a SIMPLER PROMPT, never more adjectives. Prompt text only - `services/agentLoop.mjs` and `docs/agent/masking.md`, plus tests in `tests/agent-loop.test.cjs`. NOT in scope: the agent reviewing its own result and offering a composite (blocked on MPI-887, which is what makes a composite reachable at all), and the workspace-awareness theme Fabio raised in the same conversation. Follows MPI-877.
